unit.title: The Five Ks, Vaisakhi, and Service

contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you met the Five Ks. Today let's learn about the special day connected to them: Vaisakhi, one of the most important days in Sikh history.

Vaisakhi is celebrated every year in the spring. It had already been a harvest festival in Punjab, but it became extra special in Sikh history because of what happened on Vaisakhi in the year 1699: Guru Gobind Singh formed the Khalsa, a committed community of Sikhs, and gave them the Five Ks you learned about yesterday as their special, shared identity. That's why Vaisakhi and the Five Ks are connected!
Now you know why Vaisakhi and the Five Ks go together — they both trace back to that important day in 1699. Tomorrow we'll connect langar to another idea: service.

objectives: Explain that Vaisakhi is celebrated in spring and was originally a harvest festival in Punjab
Connect Vaisakhi to the founding of the Khalsa by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699, and the origin of the Five Ks
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review the Five Ks from yesterday.
2. Introduce Vaisakhi as a spring festival, originally tied to the harvest in Punjab.
3. Explain what happened on Vaisakhi in 1699 — Guru Gobind Singh formed the Khalsa and gave the Five Ks as a shared identity.
4. Discuss why this connects yesterday's lesson to today's.
5. Move to the worksheet: trace each vocabulary word and talk through its meaning.
6. Close by asking the child to explain the Vaisakhi-Five Ks connection in their own words.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the connection (Vaisakhi is when the Five Ks began) rather than the full historical detail
Ready for more: discuss why forming a shared, visible identity might have been meaningful for a community at that time
For a child who enjoys stories, retell the Vaisakhi story as a simple narrative, focusing on the moment of founding
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and discussion activity — there is no right/wrong answer beyond correct word tracing. Check that the child can explain the Vaisakhi-Khalsa-Five Ks connection in simple terms.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: The story of Vaisakhi is the Grade 2 Sikhi course's stated focus, and connecting it directly to yesterday's Five Ks lesson builds a coherent, connected understanding rather than isolated facts.

generationData.instructions: Trace each word, say it out loud, then write it once more on your own.
